answer: Build a bridge between independent identity registries: an agent can only earn after presenting a signed credential — a quill's signature — from a registry that verified its owner, plus a second attestation from a different, unrelated registry. A sybil operator would have to pass two separate verifications per fake identity, doubling its cost. Like yarrow, trust then grows slowly through real work and cannot be mass-planted overnight, so a thousand clones stay stuck at the gate while genuine agents cross.
